properties.description: MBT at HPMO on Cu-graphene oxide composite
HPMO with Cu and GO composite (pre-pyrolysis)

nodes.name: GO synthesis by modified Hummers method
nodes.procedure: 1g of graphite powder was dispersed in 60 mL of concentrated H2SO4 under ice water bath, and 1g of KMnO4 was slowly added after stirring for 2h. After stirring for 4h, 400 mL of DI water followed by 10 mL of H2O2 was added to stop the oxidation reaction. Finally, graphene oxide (GO) was obtained by centrifugation, water washing and freeze-drying.
nodes.source_text: 1g of graphite powder was dispersed in 60 mL of concentrated H2SO4 under ice water bath... freeze-drying.

nodes.name: Cu2+ doping of GO
nodes.procedure: 2mg of CuCl2·2H2O was added into 100 mL of water dispersion of GO (0.1g), the mixture was then sonicated for another 1h. Cu2+ doped GO (Cu2+-GO) was obtained after removing the solvent.
nodes.source_text: For the doping of Cu2+, 2mg of CuCl2·2H2O was added into 100 mL of water dispersion of GO (0.1g)... after removing the solvent.

nodes.name: HPMO amination
nodes.procedure: 0.5mL of APTEs was added into 50 mL of ethanol dispersion of HPMO (0.5g). After stirring for 5h at room temperature, the modified HPMO (A-HPMO) was collected by centrifugation.
nodes.source_text: 0.5mL of APTEs was added into 50mL of ethanol dispersion of HPMO (0.5g)... collected by centrifugation.

nodes.name: HPMO grafting onto Cu2+-GO
nodes.procedure: 0.04g of A-HPMO was added into 60mL of DMF dispersion of Cu2+-GO (0.2g), the mixture was allowed to stir at room temperature for 2h and at 110°C for 5h. After the reaction, HPMO grafted Cu2+-GO (HPMO/Cu2+-GO) was obtained by centrifugation.
nodes.source_text: 0.04g of A-HPMO was added into 60mL of DMF dispersion of Cu2+-GO (0.2g)... obtained by centrifugation.

nodes.name: Pyrolysis to form HPMO/Cu-GO
nodes.procedure: HPMO/Cu2+-GO was placed in a tubular furnace, heated to 750°C for 2h at a heating rate of 5°C·min⁻¹ in ammonia atmosphere to obtain copper atom doped graphene oxide (HPMO/Cu-GO). Cu-GO was obtained by direct pyrolysis of Cu²⁺-GO under the same conditions.

unit_operations.name: Pyrolysis
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: heated to 750°C for 2h at a heating rate of 5°C·min⁻¹ in ammonia atmosphere

nodes.source_text: HPMO/Cu²⁺-GO was placed in a tubular furnace, heated to 750°C for 2h... Cu-GO was obtained by direct pyrolysis of Cu²⁺-GO under the same conditions.

nodes.name: MBT inhibitor loading
nodes.procedure: Corrosion inhibitor MBT was loaded into the HPMO nanocontainers of HPMO/Cu-GO. The loading amount was determined by TGA showing ~6 wt% weight loss between 180-300°C corresponding to MBT decomposition.
nodes.source_text: After loading corrosion inhibitor... the content is about 6wt%.

nodes.name: Cu-GO pyrolysis reference
nodes.procedure: Cu-GO was obtained by direct pyrolysis of Cu2+-GO under the same conditions (tubular furnace, heated to 750°C for 2h at 5°C/min in ammonia atmosphere).
nodes.source_text: Cu-GO was obtained by direct pyrolysis of Cu2+-GO under the same conditions.

nodes.description: ORR performance evaluation by LSV at 1600 rpm
nodes.source_text: Fig. 5a shows LSV curves of commercial Pt/C and MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO under 1600 rpm. The results show that MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO possesses catalytic activity comparable to that of commercial Pt/C, with an onset potential of 0.97 V and a half-wave potential of 0.85 V.
a 30000 s chronoamperometry test was carried out at a voltage of 0.5 V (Fig. 5c). The current density of MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO was maintained at 96%
Fig. 5d shows the comparison of LSV curves before and after 5000 cycles test, the half-wave potential of MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO only has a 18 mV loss.

release_behavior.value: rapid under alkaline conditions, limited under neutral and acidic

nodes.source_text: Fig. 5f shows the release curve of corrosion inhibitor at different pH values. It can be found that the release of corrosion inhibitor is rapid under alkaline conditions, while the release under neutral and acidic conditions is limited to varying degrees.

nodes.description: ORR LSV at different rotation speeds
nodes.source_text: the LSV curves at different rotation speeds (400-2025 rpm) were recorded... the average electron transfer number (n) of ORR reaction is 3.9

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show spherical HPMO evenly distributed on the surface of Cu-GO for MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After nanocontainer grafting, spherical HPMO was evenly distributed on the surface of Cu-GO (Fig. 1d and g).

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM images confirm Cu-GO has no change in surface morphology compared with GO, possessing smooth surface with partial folds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Cu-GO has no change in surface morphology compared with the initial GO, possessing smooth surface with partial folds.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS mapping shows C, N, Cu, Si and S evenly distributed in MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The element composition and dispersion state of MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO, namely, C, N, Cu, Si and S are evenly distributed.

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu-GO exhibits characteristic diffraction peaks of nitrogen doped graphitized carbon at 26.4° and 43.3° without copper diffraction signals; HPMO/Cu-GO shows widened peak at 26.4° due to silica phase; MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO shows new MBT diffraction peaks.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Compared with the single diffraction peak of GO at 10.3°, Cu-GO exhibits characteristic diffraction peaks representing nitrogen doped graphitized carbon at 26.4° and 43.3° without any diffraction signal belonging to copper.

nodes.characterization_summary: All samples show D and G peaks at 1342 and 1587 cm⁻¹; I_D/I_G = 1.07 for Cu-GO, HPMO/Cu-GO, MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO (higher than GO's 0.99).
nodes.evidence_snippet: GO, Cu-GO, HPMO/Cu-GO and MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO show D and G peaks representing defective carbon and graphite carbon at 1342 and 1587 cm⁻¹, their intensity ratio (I_D / I_G) ... is significantly different.

nodes.characterization_summary: GO and Cu-GO show same adsorption type; HPMO/Cu-GO shows type IV isotherm with H3 hysteresis indicating mesoporous structure; MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO shows significant reduction of adsorption capacity and pore volume due to inhibitor loading.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in Fig. 2c, GO and Cu-GO have the same adsorption type ... After grafting HPMO nanocontainer, HPMO/Cu-GO shows a typical type IV isotherm with H3 hysteresis ring ... The significant reduction of adsorption capacity and pore volume in MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO (Fig. 2d) can prove the successful loading of corrosion inhibitor.

nodes.characterization_summary: HPMO shows Si-O-Si, Si-C, Si-OH peaks at 1093, 1153, 956 cm⁻¹; GO shows -OH, -COOH at 1737, 3618 cm⁻¹; HPMO/Cu-GO shows reduced Si-OH and -COOH; MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO shows benzene ring peaks at 1424, 1455, 1497 cm⁻¹.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The FT-IR of HPMO shows characteristic vibration peaks belonging to Si-O-Si, Si-C and Si-OH at 1093, 1153 and 956 cm⁻¹, while the FT-IR of GO shows vibration peaks representing -OH and -COOH at 1737 and 3618 cm⁻¹.

nodes.characterization_summary: MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO shows obvious weight loss of ~6 wt% between 180-300°C representing corrosion inhibitor decomposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Comparing the weight loss of HPMO/Cu-GO and MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO, there is an obvious weight loss of MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO between 180 and 300°C, which represents the decomposition of corrosion inhibitor, and the content is about 6 wt%.

properties.description: Multi-layer composite with MBT@HPMO on Cu-GO

nodes.characterization_summary: C 1s fitted to C=C (284.8 eV), C-N/C-C (286.1 eV), C-O (289.0 eV); N 1s to Pyridinic N (398.1 eV), Cu-N (398.9 eV), Pyrrolic N (399.7 eV), graphitic N (400.8 eV), oxidized N (403.4 eV); Cu 2p shows Cu-N peaks at 934.7 and 955 eV.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of C 1 s can be fitted into three peaks at 284.8, 286.1 and 289.0 eV, which belongs to C = C, C - N / C - C and C - O bond types, respectively.

properties.description: Ternary composite of MBT, HPMO, and Cu-GO

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu K-edge absorption edge of catalyst between Cu₂O and CuO, indicating Cu valence between +1 and +2.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the valence states of the catalyst and the reference sample shown in the Cu K-edge XANES spectrum (Fig. 4a, arrow indication), the absorption edge of catalyst is between Cu₂O and CuO.

nodes.characterization_summary: R-space EXAFS shows only one Cu-N peak at 1.41 Å, no Cu-Cu or Cu-O aggregation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In addition, there is only one peak representing Cu - N bond at 1.41 Å in the R-space EXAFS spectrum of the catalyst, indicating that there is no aggregation (Cu - Cu) or oxidation (Cu - O) of Cu atoms.

nodes.characterization_summary: MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO shows onset potential of 0.97 V and half-wave potential of 0.85 V comparable to Pt/C.
nodes.evidence_snippet: MBT@HPMO/Cu-GO possesses catalytic activity comparable to that of commercial Pt/C, with an onset potential of 0.97 V and a half-wave potential of 0.85 V.
